source_text: Εὐσεβείας ἐπὶ πᾶσι φροντιστέον, ἣν μητέρα φασὶ τῶν ἀρετῶν, ὀρθῶς λέγοντες· αὕτη γάρ ἐστιν ἀρχὴ καὶ τελευτὴ τῶν ἀρετῶν. Τὸ εἰδέναι θεὸν καὶ τὴν πάντων συνεκτικήν τε καὶ ποιητικὴν αἰτίαν καὶ ὄψις διδάσκαλος καὶ ὁ φυσικὸς νόμος· ἡ μὲν τοῖς ὁρωμένοις προσβάλλουσα καὶ πεπηγόσιν, ὁ δὲ διʼ αὐτῶν τῶν ὁρωμένων καὶ τεταγμένων τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τούτων συλλογιζόμενος.
thought_title: Piety as beginning and end of the virtues
orientation: The work opens with a maxim on piety, then explains how knowledge of God as the sustaining and creating cause of all things is taught by sight and by the natural law.
pass_a_gloss: For piety above all things one must be concerned, which they say is mother of the virtues, speaking rightly; for this is beginning and end of the virtues. The knowing God and the all-things sustaining and creating cause both sight teaches and the natural law; the one to the things seen applying itself and to the things fixed, the other through the very things seen and ordered the author of these reasoning out.

choices.english: For piety above all things one must be concerned
choices.why: Keeps the impersonal verbal adjective force of φροντιστέον as an obligation and the fronted genitive Εὐσεβείας as the object of concern, preserving the maxim's emphasis on piety as the first duty.
rejected: One must care for piety above all
Piety must be cultivated above all things

choices.english: they say is mother of the virtues
choices.why: Retains the anarthrous predicate 'mother' and the present-tense 'they say' (φασί), matching the source's appeal to common saying without adding a definite article.
Renders the two coordinated adjectives literally as attributes of the cause, preserving the philosophical distinction between God's ongoing holding-together and His making.
rejected: the cause that holds together and creates

choices.why: Uses the fixed glossary rendering for φυσικὸς νόμος, the law by which one reasons from visible ordered things to their author.

choices.english: the author of these reasoning out
choices.why: Keeps the participle συλλογιζόμενος as 'reasoning out' to show the natural law's inferential activity, and 'author' for ἀρχηγός as the source or originator of the visible ordered things.

pass_b_english: Piety must be cultivated above all things. It is rightly called the mother of the virtues, for it is the beginning and end of the virtues. Both sight and the natural law teach us to know God, the sustaining and creating cause of all things: sight, as it falls upon visible and firmly established things; the natural law, as through those same visible and ordered things it reasons out their author.
